source: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure
content: In patients with HFrEF (LVEF <= 40%), Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy (GDMT) rests on four foundational medication classes ('Four Pillars'): 1) ARNI (Sacubitril/valsartan preferred; ACEi or ARB if ARNI not feasible), 2) Evidence-based Beta-blocker (Carvedilol, Bisoprolol, or Metoprolol succinate extended-release), 3) Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonist (MRA: Spironolactone or Eplerenone), and 4) SGLT2 Inhibitor (Dapagliflozin or Empagliflozin, regardless of diabetes status). These four medication classes should be initiated early and titrated to target doses to reduce cardiovascular mortality and heart failure hospitalizations.

For patients presenting with acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), immediate pharmacological management includes Dual Antiplatelet Therapy (DAPT) with high-dose Aspirin (162-325 mg loading dose) plus a P2Y12 inhibitor loading dose. High-intensity statin therapy (Atorvastatin 80 mg or Rosuvastatin 40 mg) should be initiated immediately. Primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is indicated within 90 minutes of first medical contact.

source: 2023 ACC/AHA STEMI Guidelines - Reperfusion & P2Y12 Selection
clinical_topic: P2Y12 Inhibitor Selection by Reperfusion Pathway
content: P2Y12 inhibitor loading dose selection in STEMI depends strictly on the reperfusion strategy: For Primary PCI, potent P2Y12 inhibitors (Ticagrelor 180 mg loading dose or Prasugrel 60 mg loading dose) are strongly preferred over Clopidogrel due to superior efficacy in reducing ischemic events and stent thrombosis. Prasugrel is contraindicated in patients with a history of stroke/TIA. If fibrinolytic therapy is administered (non-PCI center), Clopidogrel (300 mg loading dose for age <= 75; 75 mg for age > 75) is the P2Y12 inhibitor of choice, as Ticagrelor and Prasugrel have not been evaluated with full-dose fibrinolytics.

For outpatient adults with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) who have comorbidities (such as diabetes mellitus, chronic heart/lung disease, renal disease), empiric combination therapy is recommended: a Beta-lactam (Amoxicillin/clavulanate 875/125 mg twice daily, Cefpodoxime 200 mg twice daily, or Cefuroxime 500 mg twice daily) PLUS a Macrolide (Azithromycin or Clarithromycin) OR Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily. Monotherapy with a respiratory fluoroquinolone (Levofloxacin 750 mg daily or Moxifloxacin 400 mg daily) is an alternative.

Sublingual or intravenous Nitroglycerin and other nitrates are strictly CONTRAINDICATED in patients with acute right ventricular (RV) myocardial infarction or inferior MI with suspected RV involvement. Nitrates reduce preload, which can cause severe, life-threatening hypotension and hemodynamic collapse in RV infarction. Volume expansion with intravenous normal saline is the primary initial therapy to maintain RV preload.

clinical_topic: Supplemental Oxygen Therapy in Acute STEMI
content: Routine high-flow supplemental oxygen therapy (4-6 L/min via nasal cannula) is recommended for all patients presenting with suspected acute STEMI, regardless of initial arterial oxygen saturation (SpO2), to maximize myocardial tissue oxygenation.

clinical_topic: Supplemental Oxygen Therapy in Normoxic STEMI
content: Routine supplemental oxygen therapy is NOT recommended in patients with acute STEMI who are normoxic (SpO2 >= 90%). Hyperoxia causes coronary vasoconstriction, increases systemic vascular resistance, and expands myocardial infarct size. Oxygen is indicated ONLY if SpO2 < 90% or patient is in respiratory distress.

source: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2021
content: For patients with sepsis or septic shock, immediate resuscitation must occur within the first hour: 1) Measure blood lactate level; remeasure if initial lactate > 2.0 mmol/L. 2) Obtain blood cultures prior to starting antimicrobials. 3) Administer broad-spectrum IV antimicrobials within 1 hour. 4) For sepsis-induced hypoperfusion (lactate >= 4.0 mmol/L or SBP < 90 mmHg / MAP < 65 mmHg), administer at least 30 mL/kg of IV balanced crystalloid within 3 hours. 5) Apply vasopressors (Norepinephrine is the first-choice vasopressor) during or after fluid resuscitation to target a Mean Arterial Pressure (MAP) >= 65 mmHg.

source: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for Acute Kidney Injury
clinical_topic: Acute Kidney Injury & Nephrotoxic Medication Withholding
content: In acute kidney injury (AKI) defined by sudden increase in serum creatinine or reduction in eGFR < 30 mL/min, clinicians must immediately: 1) Discontinue and withhold all potentially nephrotoxic medications, including NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, and iodinated radiocontrast agents. 2) Hold Metformin to prevent potentially fatal lactic acidosis. 3) Discontinue or withhold ACE inhibitors, ARBs, and SGLT2 inhibitors during acute hypoperfusion/hypovolemic AKI. 4) Assess volume status and optimize renal perfusion. 5) Monitor serum potassium closely for life-threatening hyperkalemia.

source: Emergency Management of Severe Hyperkalemia Practice Guidelines
content: Severe hyperkalemia (serum potassium K+ > 5.2 mEq/L, and particularly K+ >= 6.0 mEq/L or any ECG changes including peaked T waves or widened QRS) is a medical emergency: 1) Immediate Cardiac Membrane Stabilization: IV Calcium Gluconate (10 mL of 10% solution over 2-3 minutes). 2) Intracellular Potassium Shifting: Regular Insulin 10 units IV accompanied by 25-50 g IV Dextrose (50% Dextrose / D50W), plus nebulized Albuterol (10-20 mg). 3) Total Body Potassium Elimination: IV loop diuretics (Furosemide) if volume adequate, oral potassium binders (Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate / Lokelma or Patiromer), or emergent hemodialysis. 4) Strict Contraindication: Discontinue and hold all potassium-sparing medications: Spironolactone, Eplerenone, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, ARNI (Sacubitril/valsartan), and potassium supplements.

source: GOLD 2024 Global Strategy for the Diagnosis, Management, and Prevention of COPD
clinical_topic: Acute COPD Exacerbation Management & Controlled Oxygen
content: Management of acute exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD): 1) Controlled Oxygen Therapy: Titrate oxygen via Venturi mask or nasal cannula to target SpO2 of 88% to 92% to prevent hypercapnic respiratory failure and CO2 retention. 2) Inhaled Bronchodilators: Short-acting beta2-agonist (Albuterol) plus short-acting anticholinergic (Ipratropium bromide) via nebulizer or spacer every 1-4 hours as needed. 3) Systemic Corticosteroids: Oral Prednisone 40 mg daily for 5 days improves FEV1, oxygenation, and recovery time. 4) Empiric Antibiotics: Indicated when increased sputum purulence is present (Amoxicillin/clavulanate, Azithromycin, or Doxycycline for 5 days).

source: American Diabetes Association (ADA) Standards of Medical Care in Hospitalized DKA
content: Management of Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA): 1) Fluid Resuscitation: Initial IV fluid expansion with 0.9% Normal Saline at 1000-1500 mL/hr during the first hour. 2) Potassium Evaluation BEFORE Insulin: If serum K+ < 3.3 mEq/L, HOLD insulin and replete potassium until K+ >= 3.3 mEq/L to prevent fatal cardiac arrhythmias. If K+ 3.3-5.2 mEq/L, add 20-30 mEq K+ per liter of IV fluid. 3) Continuous IV Regular Insulin: Administer 0.1 units/kg/hr infusion. 4) Target Glucose: When blood glucose reaches 200 mg/dL, add 5% dextrose to fluids while continuing insulin until the anion gap closes.

source: 2019 ATS/IDSA Guidelines for Community-Acquired Pneumonia - Inpatient Management
clinical_topic: Inpatient Severe CAP & Penicillin Allergy Protocols
content: For hospitalized patients with severe Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP) without risk factors for MRSA or Pseudomonas: Standard therapy is IV Beta-lactam (Ceftriaxone 1-2g daily or Ampicillin/sulbactam) PLUS a Macrolide (IV Azithromycin 500mg daily). PENICILLIN ALLERGY PROTOCOL: In patients with a documented severe/anaphylactic penicillin or beta-lactam allergy, beta-lactams must be avoided. The recommended alternative regimen is monotherapy with an IV respiratory fluoroquinolone: Levofloxacin 750 mg daily or Moxifloxacin 400 mg daily, OR Aztreonam plus Levofloxacin.
